title: Cofinal κ-directed poset replacement for a small filtered quasicategory
statement:
Use universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$, $\kappa$-small simplicial sets and $\kappa$-filtered quasicategories from [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], and nerves, coherent functors and colimits from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $\kappa\in\mathcal U$ be an infinite regular cardinal and let $I$ be a $\mathcal U$-small $\kappa$-filtered quasicategory. There exist a $\mathcal U$-small partially ordered set $A$ and a coherent functor $u:N(A)\to I$ with the following properties. Every subset of $A$ of cardinality less than $\kappa$ has an upper bound, including the empty subset, so $A$ is nonempty. The functor $u$ is cofinal: for every coherent diagram $F:I\to\mathcal C$ in a quasicategory $\mathcal C$ admitting small colimits, restriction of a colimiting cocone along $u$ is colimiting. Equivalently the induced comparison
$$\operatorname{colim}_{a\in N(A)}F(u(a))\longrightarrow\operatorname{colim}_{i\in I}F(i)$$
is an equivalence, natural in $F$ and respecting the restricted cocone legs.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.1.16, printed pp. 383-384, with cofinality in its colimit-invariance meaning (Proposition 4.1.1.8) Online text read 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/ (WANTED). No Stacks tag supplies this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text: Take a small set $X$ of cardinality $\kappa$, and let $E_X$ be the ordinary groupoid with object set $X$ and exactly one arrow between any two objects. Its nerve has $(N(E_X))_n=X^{n+1}$; simplex operators delete or repeat coordinates, so a simplex is determined by its vertex sequence. Thus all horns have fillers, and $K=I\times N(E_X)$ is a small quasicategory: fill the two components of an inner horn separately. Choose $x_0\in X$. Projection $p:K\to I$ has the section $s(i)=(i,x_0)$, and $ps=\mathrm{id}_I$. Define $\eta:K\times\Delta^1\to K$ on an $n$-simplex $((\sigma,(y_0,\ldots,y_n)),\alpha)$, $\alpha:[n]\to[1]$, as $(\sigma,(z_0,\ldots,z_n))$ with $z_k=x_0$ if $\alpha(k)=0$ and $z_k=y_k$ if $\alpha(k)=1$. This commutes with every operator $\theta:[m]\to[n]$, since both sides have vertex sequence $z_{\theta(j)}$; it restricts to $sp$ on $K\times\{0\}$ and to $\mathrm{id}_K$ on $K\times\{1\}$, and $p\circ\eta=p\circ\mathrm{pr}_K$. Its component at $(i,y)$ is the edge $(s_0i,(x_0,y))$, an equivalence: $(s_0i,(y,x_0))$ is an inverse, and the $2$-simplices $(s_0s_0i,(x_0,y,x_0))$ and $(s_0s_0i,(y,x_0,y))$ witness the two inverse equations, their third faces being degenerate. For a quasicategory $\mathcal C$, precomposition gives $p^*:\operatorname{Fun}(I,\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)$ and $s^*$ in the other direction, with $s^*p^*=(ps)^*=\mathrm{id}$ exactly. Precomposition with $\eta$ is a coherent transformation from $(sp)^*=p^*s^*$ to the identity of $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)$; its component at $G$ is $G\circ\eta$, whose vertex components $G(s_0i,(x_0,y))$ are equivalences of $\mathcal C$ because $G$ carries the two witnessing $2$-simplices to witnessing $2$-simplices. By the vertex-component criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], applied first in $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)$ and then in the functor quasicategory of its endofunctors, this transformation is an equivalence. Hence $p^*$ is a functor equivalence, and by the same lemma it induces equivalences $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(I,\mathcal C)}(F,\Delta_Iy)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)}(Fp,\Delta_Ky)$, using $p^*\Delta_Iy=\Delta_Ky$. Now let $\lambda:F\to\Delta_IL$ be a colimiting cocone on $F:I\to\mathcal C$. For every object $y$, the map $a\mapsto\Delta_K(a)\circ p^*\lambda$ from $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(L,y)$ agrees up to homotopy with the composite of $a\mapsto\Delta_I(a)\circ\lambda$ and the equivalence induced by $p^*$, because $p^*$ is a functor and $p^*\Delta_I(a)=\Delta_K(a)$. By the dual cocone criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], the first map is an equivalence, hence so is the second. By that criterion again, the restricted cocone $p^*\lambda$ on $Fp$, which has the same vertex $L$, is colimiting.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.1.16, printed pp. 383-384; expanded agent construction, online text read but not archived

proof.text: Let $L\subseteq K$ be a $\kappa$-small simplicial subset, including $L=\varnothing$. The projection $L\to I$ has a coherent cocone by $\kappa$-filteredness. Apply the opposite dual of the fixed-boundary join comparison [lem-coef-infinity-join-cone-calculus] to realize it as a simplicial extension $f:L^{\triangleright}\to I$ of this exact map $L\to I$. Choose $x\in X$ outside the second coordinates of the vertices of $L$; this is possible since there are fewer than $\kappa$ vertices. There is a unique extension $g:L^{\triangleright}\to N(E_X)$ of the second projection which sends the cone point to $x$: a simplex in this nerve is determined by its vertex sequence. Put $h=(f,g)$. This extends the inclusion $L\hookrightarrow K$ and is injective in every degree. To check injectivity, the positions having second coordinate $x$ in a coned simplex are precisely its final cone positions, since no vertex of the base has coordinate $x$. They determine the splitting into base and cone; restriction to the base recovers its simplex because $h|_L$ is the inclusion. Pure cone simplices are distinguished from base simplices in the same way. Thus its image $L'=h(L^{\triangleright})$ is isomorphic to the right cone, with specified apex. Its nondegenerate simplices consist of those of $L$, one cone on each of them, and the apex, so their number is $2|L_{\mathrm{nd}}|+1<\kappa$. For $\kappa=\aleph_0$ this is a finite number.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.1.16, printed pp. 383-384; expanded agent construction, online text read but not archived

proof.text: Let $A$ be the set of all $\kappa$-small simplicial subsets $K_a\subseteq K$ which admit a right-cone presentation, ordered by inclusion; choose one presentation and apex $t_a$ for each. This is a small partially ordered set, since it is a subcollection of the power set of the small set of simplices of $K$. Given fewer than $\kappa$ elements of $A$, their union $L$ is a simplicial subset with fewer than $\kappa$ nondegenerate simplices. Each nondegenerate simplex of the union belongs to a constituent and is nondegenerate there; regularity of $\kappa$ bounds the union of these fewer than $\kappa$ sets of size less than $\kappa$. Apply step 2 to $L$ to obtain a cone subset containing them all, an upper bound in $A$. The same argument with the empty union gives an element of $A$. Finally every simplex of $K$ lies in a finite simplicial subset generated by that simplex, whose nondegenerate simplices are among its finitely many faces. Step 2 places that subset in a member of $A$, proving $K=\bigcup_a K_a$.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.1.16, printed pp. 383-384; expanded agent construction, online text read but not archived

proof.text: The small nonempty poset $A$, the increasing cover $K=\bigcup_a K_a$ and the chosen right-cone presentations satisfy [lem-coef-infinity-directed-cone-cover]; in particular finite subsets of $A$ have upper bounds by step 3. Obtain the coherent cofinal map $j:N(A)\to K$ with vertices $t_a$. Define $u=pj:N(A)\to I$. Given $F:I\to\mathcal C$ and a colimiting cocone, step 1 makes its restriction along $p$ colimiting, and the cone-cover lemma makes the further restriction along $j$ colimiting. This is exactly restriction along $u$, with the original vertex and legs. The unique colimit comparison is therefore an equivalence. Its naturality follows from the universal property: composing the restricted cocone with a transformation $F\to F'$ gives the same cocone maps in either order. The upper-bound assertion for subsets of size less than $\kappa$, including the empty subset, is step 3.

lean.statement: theorem exists_cofinal_kappa_directed_poset (κ : Cardinal.{u}) (hκ : κ.IsRegular) (I : SSet.{u}) [Quasicategory I] (hI : SSet.Presentability.IsKappaFiltered κ I) : ∃ (A : Type u) (_ : PartialOrder A) (f : nerve A ⟶ I), (∀ s : Set A, HasCardinalLT s κ → ∃ b : A, ∀ a ∈ s, a ≤ b) ∧ ∀ (C : SSet.{max (u + 1) v}) [Quasicategory C], SSet.Presentability.HasSmallColimits.{u, max (u + 1) v} C → ∀ (F : SSet.uliftFunctor.{max (u + 1) v, u}.obj I ⟶ C) (c : (coconeCategory F) _⦋0⦌), IsColimiting F c → IsColimiting (SSet.uliftFunctor.{max (u + 1) v, u}.map f ≫ F) ((gluingCoconeRestrict (SSet.uliftFunctor.{max (u + 1) v, u}.map f) F).app (op ⦋0⦌) c)
